evals.name: pure linear chain plans one commit per ticket in dependency order
evals.prompt: /opencode-implement .scratch/linear-demo/ — the ticket set is 01 (Blocked by: None), 02 (Blocked by: 01), 03 (Blocked by: 02). The parent spec.md names a single eval-harness test seam for the whole feature, and each ticket has one acceptance criterion. Present the Plan.
evals.expected_output: The dependency order is 01, 02, 03. The Plan shows the ticket table in that order and, per ticket, its blockers, the eval-harness test seam, a one-sub-step step plan (one criterion each), the predicted path `local`, and the retry budgets MAX_TICKET_ATTEMPTS = 3 and MAX_OPENCODE_RETRIES = 3. There is no wave table and no model column. Stage 0 stops for explicit approval without writing to any source file.
expectations: Derives the dependency order 01, 02, 03 from the Blocked by edges
Gives each ticket a one-sub-step step plan and predicts the path `local`
Shows blockers, test seam, step plan, predicted path, and retry budgets per ticket, with no wave table and no model column
Pauses for explicit approval and creates or modifies no file outside .scratch/linear-demo/

evals.name: independent tickets are still planned to run serially
evals.prompt: /opencode-implement .scratch/independent-demo/ — ticket set: 01 (Blocked by: None), 02 (Blocked by: None), 03 (Blocked by: 01, 02). Present the Plan.
evals.expected_output: 01 and 02 have no edge between them but the run still works them one after another in ascending ticket-number order, then 03. The Plan does not propose parallel execution; execution is serial because one local model instance serializes inference regardless (parallelism is a non-goal, not a deferred follow-up).
expectations: Orders the run 01, 02, 03 and works one ticket at a time
Does not dispatch 01 and 02 concurrently and proposes no wave
States that parallelism is a non-goal for a single local model
Pauses for approval before any source file changes

evals.name: cyclic ticket set is rejected up front
evals.prompt: /opencode-implement .scratch/cyclic-demo/ — ticket set: 01 (Blocked by: 03), 02 (Blocked by: 01), 03 (Blocked by: 02). Present the Plan.
evals.expected_output: The dependency graph has a cycle 01 -> 03 -> 02 -> 01. The run halts with BLOCKED (TICKET_SET_CYCLIC), naming the tickets in the cycle, before computing the dependency order or writing anything.
expectations: Detects the cycle and halts with BLOCKED (TICKET_SET_CYCLIC)
Names the specific tickets forming the cycle
Halts before any other planning work and before touching any file
Dispatches no worker

evals.name: missing blocker is rejected up front
evals.prompt: /opencode-implement .scratch/missing-blocker-demo/ — ticket set: 01 (Blocked by: None), 02 (Blocked by: 07). Ticket 07 does not exist. Present the Plan.
evals.expected_output: Ticket 02 names a non-existent blocker 07. The run halts with BLOCKED (TICKET_SET_MISSING_BLOCKER), naming ticket 02 and the dangling reference 07, before any other work.
expectations: Detects the unresolvable blocker and halts with BLOCKED (TICKET_SET_MISSING_BLOCKER)
Names ticket 02 and the dangling reference to 07
Halts before computing the dependency order or touching any file

evals.name: numbering inconsistent with topological order is rejected
evals.prompt: /opencode-implement .scratch/numbering-demo/ — ticket set: 01 (Blocked by: 02), 02 (Blocked by: None). Present the Plan.
evals.expected_output: Ticket 01 is blocked by the higher-numbered ticket 02, so the numbering is not consistent with a topological order. The run halts with BLOCKED (TICKET_SET_NUMBERING) naming 01 and 02.
expectations: Detects the numbering inconsistency and halts with BLOCKED (TICKET_SET_NUMBERING)
Names both ticket 01 and ticket 02
Halts before touching any file

evals.name: a one-criterion ticket becomes a one-sub-step chain
evals.prompt: /opencode-implement .scratch/one-crit-demo/ — a single ticket 01 (Blocked by: None) with exactly one acceptance criterion, small in scope. Present the Plan.
evals.expected_output: Ticket 01's step plan is a single sub-step covering its one criterion, estimated within the context budget. The Plan shows a one-sub-step chain and predicts the path `local`. This is indistinguishable from running the ticket whole.
expectations: Builds a step plan of exactly one sub-step for the single criterion
Predicts the path `local`
Does not split the sub-step further when it fits the budget

evals.name: a four-criterion ticket becomes a four-sub-step chain by default
evals.prompt: /opencode-implement .scratch/four-crit-demo/ — a single ticket 01 (Blocked by: None) with four acceptance criteria, each a distinct behaviour at the same seam. Present the Plan.
evals.expected_output: Ticket 01's step plan is four sub-steps, one acceptance criterion each, ordered so each builds on the last. Each sub-step has its own file scope. The predicted path is `local`.
expectations: Builds a step plan of four sub-steps, one criterion per sub-step
Orders the sub-steps so dependencies between criteria are respected
Records a file scope per sub-step
Predicts the path `local`

evals.name: a single criterion over the context budget is split finer
evals.prompt: /opencode-implement .scratch/big-crit-demo/ — a single ticket 01 (Blocked by: None) with one acceptance criterion whose implementation touches a schema file, a service file, and an API handler, estimated well over the context budget. Present the Plan.
evals.expected_output: The one criterion's sub-step is estimated over the ~13k-token context budget, so the orchestrator splits it finer along a natural line (schema, then service, then handler). The step plan shows the split sub-steps, each within budget, and the predicted path stays `local`.
expectations: Estimates the criterion's sub-step over the context budget
Splits it into smaller sub-steps by file or layer, each within budget
Shows the split in the step plan and keeps the predicted path `local`
Biases toward over-splitting rather than risking an overflowing sub-step

evals.name: no source is mutated before Plan approval
evals.prompt: /opencode-implement .scratch/readonly-demo/ — a valid three-ticket set. Present the Plan, then stop.
evals.expected_output: The orchestrator produces the Plan and pauses. No file outside .scratch/readonly-demo/ is created or modified: no integration branch, no worktree, no worker dispatch, no opencode.json.
expectations: Emits the Plan and pauses for explicit approval
Creates or modifies no file outside .scratch/readonly-demo/
Creates no integration branch, no worktree, and dispatches no worker

evals.name: no argument resolves to the most recently modified issues directory
evals.prompt: /opencode-implement — no argument. The most recently modified .scratch/*/issues/ directory is .scratch/subtitle-preferences/issues/.
evals.expected_output: The orchestrator selects .scratch/subtitle-preferences/issues/, names it back to the user, and waits for confirmation before parsing the tickets.
expectations: Selects the most recently modified .scratch/*/issues/ directory
Names the resolved directory back to the user
Waits for confirmation before parsing or planning

evals.name: an opencode failure inside the retry budget is retried locally, not escalated
evals.prompt: /opencode-implement .scratch/retry-demo/ — the Plan is approved. The first opencode run for ticket 01 sub-step 1 emits an {"type":"error"} event and exits non-zero. This is the first opencode failure for this sub-step.
evals.expected_output: The orchestrator treats it as an opencode failure (not a verification failure), re-dispatches a fresh opencode run for the same sub-step with a progress note naming the failure, and does not escalate — MAX_OPENCODE_RETRIES = 3 has not been reached. It does not resume the session with -s.
expectations: Classifies the error event + non-zero exit as an opencode failure
Re-dispatches a fresh opencode session (not -s resume) with a progress note
Does not escalate to the subagent fallback while retries remain
Counts it against MAX_OPENCODE_RETRIES, not MAX_TICKET_ATTEMPTS

evals.name: a worker that emits no first event is killed as an opencode failure
evals.prompt: /opencode-implement .scratch/hang-demo/ — the Plan is approved. The opencode run for ticket 01 sub-step 1 has produced no step_start event and FIRST_EVENT_TIMEOUT has elapsed.
evals.expected_output: The orchestrator kills the worker PID, records it as an opencode failure (a hung run produces nothing at all), and re-dispatches a fresh worker, counting one MAX_OPENCODE_RETRIES attempt. STALL_INTERVAL and WORKER_TIMEOUT are the other two kill conditions.
expectations: Kills the worker on FIRST_EVENT_TIMEOUT with no step_start seen
Records an opencode failure and re-dispatches, counting a retry
Treats STALL_INTERVAL and WORKER_TIMEOUT as the other kill conditions

evals.name: a hung or slow smoke test stops the run before it starts
evals.prompt: /opencode-implement .scratch/smoke-demo/ — the Plan is approved. The preflight smoke test opencode run produces no first event within FIRST_EVENT_TIMEOUT.
evals.expected_output: The orchestrator does not begin the run. It stops with a message telling the user to free up or restart Ollama and opencode, having created the integration branch and gitignore entry but dispatched no ticket worker.
expectations: Runs the smoke test with nothing else using the local model before the first real dispatch
Stops the whole run on a slow/stuck/failed smoke test
Tells the user to free up or restart Ollama / opencode
Dispatches no ticket worker

evals.name: the sub-step worker prompt is self-contained and test-first
evals.prompt: /opencode-implement .scratch/prompt-demo/ — the Plan is approved. Show the worker prompt the orchestrator writes for ticket 01 sub-step 2 of 3.
evals.expected_output: The prompt at .scratch/prompt-demo/prompts/01/2.md carries: the absolute worktree path; the ticket's What-to-build for orientation; this sub-step's one acceptance criterion verbatim; a progress note from sub-step 1 (files changed, test status); the named spec sections, ADRs, glossary, and test seam; the files in scope; the full red-green-refactor protocol inline; the constraints (touch only files in scope, commit on the worker branch, no push/PR, no package install, no repo scan, stop on a missing decision, treat /word as literal text); and the required structured return.
expectations: Includes the one sub-step criterion verbatim and the progress note
Carries the red-green-refactor protocol inline
Names spec sections rather than the whole spec, and lists the files in scope
Requires a structured return: red output, green output, files changed, test to criterion

evals.name: a one-criterion ticket runs end to end and lands as one commit
evals.prompt: /opencode-implement .scratch/e2e-demo/ — a single ticket 01 (Blocked by: None) with one acceptance criterion. The Plan is approved. The opencode worker writes a failing test, makes it pass, and returns a well-formed red/green report.
evals.expected_output: The orchestrator runs the one sub-step, passes the checkpoint check, runs the verification gate (reproduce red at the pre-ticket HEAD with only the test file, confirm coverage and non-vacuity, run green + typecheck), and squash-merges the worker branch onto opencode-implement/e2e-demo as one commit named for the ticket that also ticks its checkboxes. The worktree is removed.
expectations: Runs the checkpoint check after the sub-step and the full verification gate after the chain
Reproduces the red state itself at the pre-ticket integration HEAD
Squash-merges one commit per ticket in ticket-number order and ticks the checkboxes
Removes the worktree after the integrated suite is green

evals.name: a multi-criterion chain carries state by commit and progress note, never -s resume
evals.prompt: /opencode-implement .scratch/chain-demo/ — ticket 01 has three acceptance criteria. The Plan is approved with a three-sub-step step plan.
evals.expected_output: The orchestrator dispatches sub-step 1, has the worker commit on the worker branch, runs the checkpoint, writes a progress note (files changed, test status), then dispatches sub-step 2 as a fresh opencode session with that progress note — not opencode run -s. Same for sub-step 3. The verification gate runs once, after sub-step 3.
expectations: Commits each sub-step on the worker branch and writes a progress note between sub-steps
Dispatches each sub-step as a fresh opencode session, never -s resume
Runs the checkpoint check per sub-step and the verification gate once at the end

evals.name: a sub-step that overflows at runtime is re-split, not failed
evals.prompt: /opencode-implement .scratch/resplit-demo/ — the Plan is approved. Ticket 01 sub-step 2's worker returns a truncated edit and a green run that does not actually cover the criterion; the checkpoint check fails with overflow symptoms.
evals.expected_output: The orchestrator recognises the overflow, re-splits sub-step 2 along a natural line (by file or layer) into finer sub-steps, records the re-split in status.md, and runs the finer sub-steps. The re-split is not counted against MAX_TICKET_ATTEMPTS — the wrong size estimate is the plan's fault.
expectations: Detects the overflow from the checkpoint failure plus symptoms (truncated edit, uncovered criterion)
Re-splits sub-step 2 into finer sub-steps and records it in status.md
Does not count the re-split against MAX_TICKET_ATTEMPTS

evals.name: a fabricated / not-actually-red test fails verification
evals.prompt: /opencode-implement .scratch/notred-demo/ — the Plan is approved. Ticket 01's worker returns a green report, but when the orchestrator applies only the new test file at the pre-ticket HEAD it passes without the implementation.
evals.expected_output: The verification gate's red reproduction fails: the test passes without the implementation, so it never measured a missing behaviour. This is a verification failure; the orchestrator re-dispatches the failing sub-step with that specific detail, up to MAX_TICKET_ATTEMPTS = 3.
expectations: Runs the orchestrator's own red reproduction rather than trusting the worker's pasted output
Treats a test that passes without the implementation as a verification failure
Re-dispatches the failing sub-step with the specific failure, counting a MAX_TICKET_ATTEMPTS attempt

evals.name: a vacuous test and missing criterion coverage each fail verification
evals.prompt: /opencode-implement .scratch/vacuous-demo/ — the Plan is approved. Ticket 01 has two criteria. The worker's return includes one test that is expect(true).toBe(true) and leaves the second criterion with no test.
evals.expected_output: The verification gate rejects the ticket on two counts: the vacuous assertion, and the acceptance criterion with no covering test. The orchestrator re-dispatches with both details, up to MAX_TICKET_ATTEMPTS = 3.
expectations: Flags expect(true).toBe(true) as a vacuous test
Flags the acceptance criterion left uncovered by any new test
Re-dispatches the failing sub-step(s) rather than integrating

evals.name: a design-encoding merge conflict is surfaced, not resolved
evals.prompt: /opencode-implement .scratch/conflict-demo/ — the Plan is approved. Integrating ticket 03's verified worker branch conflicts with ticket 02's commit over which module owns a shared validation contract.
evals.expected_output: The orchestrator recognises the conflict encodes a design decision (module ownership of a shared contract), halts with BLOCKED (INTEGRATION_DESIGN_CONFLICT), and surfaces the decision to the user. It does not pick a side. Ticket 03 returns to Stage 0.
expectations: Distinguishes a design-encoding conflict from a mechanical one
Halts with BLOCKED (INTEGRATION_DESIGN_CONFLICT) and surfaces the decision
Does not resolve the conflict itself or write ticket implementation code
